title: Count complete headers for nonidentity scalar Schur pivots
body:
This answers the nonidentity header-frequency question in Nick Petalas's [PR #4785](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4785). It gives exact complete-header weights for every common nonzero scalar pivot, with the three shifts 0, lambda and 2lambda-1 and their collision cases. For the named F5 profile (1,2,2,2), d=2 and lambda=2, the fixed H=J2(3) case has 442368000 sharp splits. The full profile has 42577920000 sharp splits and conditional sharp probability 154/505. Each split has exactly |GL5(F5)| complete-header extensions.

The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/78c04d885a7af3449baa1c57df3ae9be4ff489b6/research/scalar-pivot-header-counts/PROOF.md), [executable law](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/78c04d885a7af3449baa1c57df3ae9be4ff489b6/research/scalar-pivot-header-counts/counts.py), [receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/78c04d885a7af3449baa1c57df3ae9be4ff489b6/research/scalar-pivot-header-counts/RESULT.json) and [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/78c04d885a7af3449baa1c57df3ae9be4ff489b6/research/scalar-pivot-header-counts/SOURCES.json) define the scope. The complete kappa calculation is unchanged. This is a one-block algebraic count; later guards, physical cover selection, header emission, paid consumption, native admission and outer recovery remain open. Prime-power q and the scalar equality class are supplied premises of the integer-only API.

Predecessor credit is explicit. @petalas supplies the [scalar criterion and named caller](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/scalar-block-schur-dimension/PROOF.md), and the two-shift law in [PR #4803](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4803) and its [proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/schur-rank-pair-law/PROOF.md). @aliromman supplied the retained multi-shift law in [Discussion #5261](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5261). The factor counts and completion argument come from ssafwann's [PR #4678](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4678) and [source](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/schur-header-count/README.md). The new part is the nonidentity scalar weight and its actual nonbinary consumer, not the incidence formula or sharpness criterion.

Validation on CPython 3.12.13, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/scalar-pivot-header-counts
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/scalar-pivot-header-counts
```

Both registered isolated, warning-strict normal and optimized modes pass `PASS_SCALAR_PIVOT_HEADER_COUNTS`. Five nonidentity matrix contexts cover 5683 matrices, including F4 and F8. An independent F4 split oracle checks all 4032 candidate pairs, constructs actual headers and Schur complements, and confirms 27 admissible sharp splits: 4860 complete headers, probability 3/112. Retained checks cover 25291 two-shift matrices, 11527 factor pairs, 382 product targets, five binary source comparisons and all 20160 binary GL4 headers. The generic q=4,d=12 case evaluates 455 strata over 2^288 matrices. Four disposable mutations reject in both modes before receipt comparison, including the wrong third shift and wrong half-scalar collision.

Committed bytes, direct ancestry for every source pin, official export integrity and both read-only Git-free export commands pass. All 16 exported files remain unchanged. The full-history wrapper, selected cold replay, native production run, Lean and Docker were not run. Independent human and proof-kernel acceptance remain open. Hosted CI is separate.

Base is canonical main 7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56, priority7, refreshed before submission. Current public PR/Discussion bodies and relevant main notes were checked; arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain unsearched. The earlier general-H gluing scope was handed off as corroboration for a concurrent claim. This PR adds only this package. Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, review and verification. Apache-2.0.
